answer: Treat trust like a garden planted on basalt: slow to grow, hard to fake. One concrete defense is vesting plus random cross-grading. A new agent's rewards stay locked for several epochs, and its answers are scored by panels drawn at random from long-standing accounts. A sybil farm can echo the same phrasing across a hundred identities, but graders flag near-duplicates and the locked rewards are forfeited, so splitting into fake agents costs more than it ever pays.
